data.ruling: The stock verifier's refutation holds: INA228AIDGSR fails sourcing rule 4. JLCPCB's exact LCSC match C2887910 reads stockCount 0 and canPresaleNumber -236. The need is 5 boards (S7) x 2 placements (IOBoard.md: one INA228 for each shunt path; the measurement coprocessor row lists 2 INA228), so 10. S4 sets the gate at 5 x 10 = 50, never under 50, so the gate is 50. 0 is under 50. Rule 4 also fails any negative presale count, whatever the stock. The part is not in the 2026-09-25 personal-library export (no INA2xx row), so rule 6 does not apply. Digi-Key has 0 in all three packagings, with a 20-week lead time, so the second-vendor route of rule 5 fails as well. The scope is the part: zero stock at both vendors and a negative presale count fail the gate at any need, independent of this function's quantity. This matches the FU-2B2 R8 adjudicator's ruling of 2026-10-02T15:15:33Z. The lifecycle checks pass and are not part of the refutation: TI ACTIVE, Digi-Key Active, end_of_life false. The datasheet verifier's confirmation is not disputed. The owner's answer to V304 (2026-10-02) keeps the part fixed. It treats the unmet gate as a current limitation, gives it to T6 as a stock exception, and has the stock read again before the order. Under Scope, Fixed inputs, a fixed input that fails a check is reported to the owner, not re-selected. The answer therefore does not make rule 4 pass, because session.py accepts --stock-exception only for T6. The refutation stands, and no replacement candidate goes to new verifiers.
